page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, operating with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. It is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A defining hardware characteristic is its integrated local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and weak single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1102.49, which is in the bottom 25 percent, while the multi-core CPU test reaches 8789.97, placing it in the middle 50 percent. Single-threaded gzip compression is poor at 18.96 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 7.41 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the average tier at 37.67 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed, with a weak PassMark memory score of 1685.71, though large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths maintain average ratings at 54.9 GB/sec and 47.08 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 8.27 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.3xlarge lies in its storage medium and CPU generation. While it offers a massive local HDD storage capacity of over 35 TB, the use of traditional HDD technology limits random I/O performance compared to modern solid-state drives. The older Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 architecture delivers moderate multi-threaded compute capabilities but lags in single-core efficiency. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides high storage density per resource unit, making it suitable for workloads requiring large-capacity sequential data storage rather than high-speed random access. Appropriate workloads include cold data storage, large-scale log processing, data archiving, and sequential-access database operations.

Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.
